verdict.tagline: Slash blocks to a beat, but prepare for broken mods.
for_you_if: you want a high-energy workout powered by music
you plan to dive into custom community tracks
you enjoy rhythm games requiring fast reflexes
not_for_you_if: you are not willing to deal with updates breaking mods
you dislike paying extra for additional song packs
you expect a massive native song catalog

cohorts.label: <2h refund window
cohorts.summary: Early players encounter censored tracks and mods that break with patches.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that official songs in the game or its DLC are censored.

citations.review_text: game is good, but they censor official songs... (like linkin park given up from dlc)

Back when this came out it was a masterpiece of a game.
Now, 6 years on, it's a bottomless pit of absurdly priced "DLC" (aka song packs).
There are mods that make it better, for example allowing you to download additional songs & user created levels. But those mods frequently get broken when the game is updated to a new version (I assume this is purposeful by the devs), so if you go down this route I recommend you google how to install an older (mod friendly) version of the game and how to set things up so that you stay on that version. You lose out on "updates" but those are almost exclusively overpriced music packs so you're not really missing out.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the base game has a thin song catalog, requiring purchases of additional DLC song packs or the use of community mods for long-term play.

citations.review_text:
Beat Saber is probably the most known VR game out there and it still holds up as one of the first thing people try when they get into VR

The base catalog is honestly pretty thin though, unless you're ready to drop money on DLC packs to actually have something to play long term. And even after all these years the game feels weak on the features side, no real leaderboards, no extra polish, you basically need mods and plugins just to get stuff that feels almost mandatory in 2026

Still, once the saber is in your hand none of that really matters, it stays fun every single time and it's the game you hand to anyone who just got a headset

Probably the only VR game i enjoy playing from time to time, the interface is simple and polished, no weird buttons to press unlike 99% of VR games. In my opinion, if you own a VR, Beat Saber is a must have, whether you're playing it by yourself, or you want to make fun of your friends while they're wobbling in your living room.

The only issue is the lack of songs at the beginning, which is solvable but requires some time.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game lacks a built-in browser or tool for adding custom songs, requiring external modding to access community tracks.

citations.review_text: its so much fun but honestly its only worth it for the modded songs and it really is a shame theres no steam workshop integration

Beat Saber is a fantastic game, if you figure out how to install mods.
This is one of those VR games that can almost justify buying a headset on its own. In many ways, it's a VR classic. The concept is simple: hit blocks to the rhythm of music. But it works incredibly well because the gameplay feels perfectly suited to VR. You're moving your arms, following the beat, and physically interacting with the music instead of just pressing buttons. It's easy to learn and consistently fun to play.
The biggest problem is the developers' greed. There is no built in way to browse and download custom songs, so you're expected to either buy DLC packs separately or instal mods. Seriously, it’s the same level of supervillainous greed as Paradox Interactive with their Stellaris. The DLC library is huge, but there is no guarantee it will contain the music you're actually interested in.
Thankfully, mods solve this problem and make the game significantly better. The only downside is that setting them up can be more complicated than it should be, especially for a VR game.
Despite that, Beat Saber remains one of the best VR games available and an easy recommendation for anyone with a headset.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that community-made maps suffer from an extreme lack of easier difficulty options, as user-created content leans heavily into unbalanced or expert-level charts.

citations.review_text:
I was really hoping i could find something in this game, but I guess not. If you're not exactly great at these kind of games and just want to have fun and enjoy your favorite songs then you can forget about this.

I haven't gotten to play the base game songs, and I never really cared about them at all, not my kind of music.
Songs that I wanted play are ALL either unbalanced, Expert or higher. I tried, I really did but there's an extreme lack of easier maps in the community-made maps.
Even if you really want to try and get better at this - there's not much to play other than the base game songs. 
That's something that I wouldn't find to be fun in particular.

DLCs also seem to be absolute garbage but it's not that I cared about those in the first place.

[This review comes from a longtime quest player, so most of my hours are there]

This game on itself is just, fine.
You kinda need to play modded or else the 30 bucks you spent on this game will never be worth it
Meta bought the game and ruined it for everyone,
focusing on DLC packs instead of the free OST packs and there's no variety with the OST packs 
the same three or four artists with the same sound all throughout

Beat saber peaked in OST 5, most songs, most variety
feels like new songs also don't care about people who want to have fun, 
expert+ became less about fun but skill, which I don't mind obviously but newer maps feel like you have to twist your bones to hit notes, like the difficulty is intended for those that DO play modded

meanwhile, DLC maps get the songs people DO want and with actual good, fun mapping 
I just can't get into the flow with OST maps

Modded adds alot of QoL features and makes the game actually enjoyable, you get actual songs that you want
and the option to do ranked (featuring a pp system like osu)

I'm genuinely disappointed about the state of the game right now, however it's still a lot of fun modded

and ever since meta bought the game, the game has been horribly mistreated on Steam - this game hasn't been on sale in YEARS - it only went on sale ONCE, meanwhile the game constantly goes on sale on the horizon platform, and sometimes even given out for free (if you get the 30 dollars from their referral program)

they've constantly made it harder to mod the game on the quest, you NEED a computer to mod it now.

TL;DR
10/10 game, meta ruined the main game, play modded.

P.S. OST 8 sucks, and the new extra 3 songs are just sad - 8th year anniversary and we only get scraps.
Screw you, Meta.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game never goes on sale.

citations.review_text:
Its an incredible game! Really enjoying it on my Quest 2 through PCVR Steamlink. 

Being able to add user made songs and maps has really boosted this game up for me too. The price tag and lack of sales made it a tougher pill to swallow but the user maps really pushed my enjoyment of this to an 11 and got me to purchase more songs to boot since I wanted more great levels!
Never goes on sale so don't wait around. Custom maps are the way to go.

fun game, as long as you know how to mod the game, consider beatleader + scoresaber too if you want to be in a competitive community and climb leaderboards
- game feels very vanilla without mods but unless you REALLY like the songs, i personally don't recommend buying song packs since they're like $2 (usd) a song, would probably suggest adding custom songs instead 
- the game also quite literally never goes on sale (except for that one time it was $20, but this was shortly after its launch)

ig on the bright side you can at least have a good workout from beat saber from doing fitbeat-styled charts, you also don't need a super beefy computer to run the game, you just need a pc that can run vr

[spoiler] it's been nearly half a decade and they STILL haven't released custom sabers yet [/spoiler]

It's the best workout I've ever tricked myself into doing, and after a few hundred hours it's still the only game I boot up in VR. My one real gripe is is the DLC pricing, which gets absurd fast. If you are like me learn how to mod it for custom songs because that's where the PC game truly opens up. Vanilla is fun, but modded is what keeps people here for years. Grab it, if is your first time do the campaign and then mod, but always remember to clear some space around you first.

The game has mods (just not on steam), and also it is very well made. It still gets updates, new vanilla maps, and it has 5 difficulties so you will certainly find something interesting for you. claims.claim: Reviewers report that game updates break mods.

citations.review_text: Fun game with mods and custom levels. Just annoying a lot of the time updates cause issues with them.

i used to love the game but since facebook bought them up its gone to ♥♥♥♥. mods breaking on every update, the game becoming a cash grab and most importantly: the bugs. in the old versions all the notes hit when youd expect them to and now half the time they wont register. i verified it in replays over multiple versions where my saber was inside the note and should have hit from the motion but the game ignored it. im used to playing on a high difficulty which is unable to be played without mods so i have to choose one version of the game and stick to that and since most mods are on newer versions i sadly have to play those versions but since the game dosent register the notes as it should i sadly cannot play the difficulty i want to play without downgrading. if you decide to play the game please use something like bsmanager to make your life easier and play an older version(before 1.40). and for those who say "why dont you play the hard songs from the official maps?": the official songs are so easy calling them "expert+" is a joke.

It's hard to get into a flow when I slice clean through a block that's right in front of my face, and it registers a miss.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the base game song selection as limited and bland, noting that community-made custom songs and mods are necessary to get the most out of the experience.

citations.review_text: Truly the bread and butter of VR, the official maps are pretty bland and uncreative, but with easily installed custom songs, it's one of the greatest VR experiences to date. It's cheap enough to justify purchasing when you're already spending hundreds or thousands on a headset in the first place, and as long as you aren't getting ripped off by paying for official music packs, it's a great time.

Beat Saber is easily one of the best VR games out there with super fun and satisfying gameplay that never gets old. My only real complaint is that the base song selection feels limited and there are a lot of paid song packs, which can get expensive, but thankfully the modding community completely fixes that with custom songs and tons of extra content that make the game even more amazing overall.
I’m just here for the custom songs and mods. Official maps have been historically lackluster, but the community-made content lets you tailor your Beat Saber experience to your liking.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that game updates break mods, requiring players to lock in legacy versions to maintain mod compatibility.

citations.review_text:
-Price
-Updates forcing to play without mods
-DLC (give me your wallet) Bonanza

Good game, bad experience ever since devs went full sellout years ago. It's the classic early access cycle of get a hit, get bought out, and then stop caring about the actual players. You CAN still enjoy this game with mods + custom songs, but you need to go to the settings -> betas -> and lock in one of the legacy versions. (stay around 1.29.1 or 1.32 if you want a stable experience).

MODS ARE THE ONLY REASON THIS GAME SURVIVES. Period. Devs are lazy, they just pump out DLC packs and call it a day, DLC songs will get yanked from your library by copyright holders when deals fall though (many other reviews mention this aswell - thats right that song you paid for? gone! because fk you.) Oh, and like with most of the music industry, its not even clear that those tracks you bought even pay the actual artists...

But the worst part? The gameplay got more difficult for no reason, in later versions beyond ~1.32 new "features" were to cater to expert+ sweatlords - and THEN whoever they had the audacity of hiring to map the songs sucked donkey balls - the rhythm is off on ALL difficulties but expert+ maps mostly need you to RECALIBRATE YOUR AUDIO SYNC ON EVERY FKIN MAP. its TRASH.

IF you know how to mod/want to spend the time, this is still a good VR app, as long as Steam lets you get the older files... otherwise I cannot recommend it in current state.
